title: Public company research
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for researching public companies from official sources: filings fetched through the SEC's EDGAR APIs under its fair-access rules and investor-relations releases read as their terms permit, metrics with the filing, period and unit behind every number, period and peer comparisons, risk factor summaries, a dated catalyst calendar and a cited brief that is not financial advice, places no trades or orders, and leaves every decision to a person.
boundaries: Not financial advice: outputs describe what official sources say and never recommend, rate or target.
No trades or orders: no verb places, stages or routes an order or reaches a brokerage.
Official sources only, read under each provider's terms; for SEC EDGAR, a declared User-Agent and a rate well under its limit.
A person decides what is delivered; importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for researching public companies from official sources, never as financial advice

value.lets_workers: Research a public company from official sources: fetch its filings through the SEC's EDGAR APIs under the SEC's fair-access rules and read its investor-relations releases as their terms permit, extract metrics with the filing, period and unit behind every number, compare periods and peers, summarize risk factors, build a dated catalyst calendar, and write a cited brief marked Not financial advice. A different worker reviews every number, and a person decides what is delivered. No verb trades or places an order.
value.worked_example: Made-up: a fictional outdoor retailer and a peer, with a derived fourth quarter, a restated prior year, a reworded and a new risk factor, two filing deadlines computed by rule, and a brief the library's tests recompute.

nouns.title: Guardrail: not financial advice
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Describe what filings and company releases say. Never recommend buying, selling or holding a security, never give a price target, a rating or a position size, and never say what anyone should do with their money. Every brief carries the notice Not financial advice.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every brief's notice is exactly Not financial advice, and no point matches the advice phrases in the brief checks.

nouns.title: Guardrail: no trades or orders
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: No verb places, stages, previews or routes a trade or an order, connects to a brokerage or trading account, or holds brokerage credentials. A request to trade ends blocked with a plain refusal.
value.how_it_is_checked: No verb's network mode reaches a brokerage or trading host, no output has an order field, and no point matches the order phrases in the brief checks.

nouns.title: Guardrail: cite every number
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Every number names its source: the filer's CIK, the form and accession number, the fiscal period, the XBRL concept or the document section, the unit, and the date it was read. A derived number shows its formula and the cited numbers it came from. A company-defined measure that GAAP does not define is labeled as such and kept out of GAAP tables.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every figure in a metric table and every number in a brief resolves to a cited fact or to a derivation from cited facts.

nouns.title: Guardrail: respect each data provider's terms
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Read each data provider only as its terms permit. For SEC EDGAR: its documented APIs and archives, a User-Agent that declares the requester's organization and contact email, a request rate well under its published limit of 10 per second in total, and only what the request needs. For a company's investor-relations pages: read their terms of use first, use no login, and stop when the terms forbid automated reading. Use third-party prices or estimates only under a license the requester holds, and never copy them into a shared noun.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every source in a filing index records its access method, the date its terms were read, that a User-Agent was declared, and its request count and peak rate.

nouns.title: Reading SEC EDGAR fairly
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

endpoints.bulk: companyfacts.zip and submission.zip, republished nightly at about 3:00 a.m. ET

rules: The CIK in an API address is 10 digits with leading zeros. The APIs need no key.
Declare a User-Agent with the requester's organization and contact email, in the SEC's sample format.
Stay well under 10 requests per second across every machine the requester runs; this pack's default is 2.
Fetch only what the request needs: one company facts call instead of many concept calls, and the bulk files for many companies.
Cache every response, record its SHA-256, and reuse it instead of fetching it again.
On a 403 or 429, or a page saying the request rate threshold was exceeded, stop, back off and resume more slowly. Never rotate addresses or present a browser's User-Agent.
Use only the documented APIs and archives.

nouns.title: Metric definitions and period rules
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

reported.revenue: Revenues, or RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax; record which concept the company uses.

derived.growth_percent: (current minus prior) divided by prior, times 100
derived.gross_margin_percent: gross profit divided by revenue, times 100
derived.operating_margin_percent: operating income divided by revenue, times 100
derived.free_cash_flow: operating cash flow minus capital expenditure; derived, not a reported GAAP measure
derived.fourth_quarter: the fiscal year's value minus the nine-month year-to-date value from the third-quarter Form 10-Q; derived

rules: Compare like with like: a fiscal year with a fiscal year, a quarter with the same quarter a year earlier.
Duration facts carry a start and an end date; instant facts carry one date.
When a later filing restates a period, use the latest filed value and list the earlier one with both accession numbers.
Keep raw values exactly as filed, with their units. Round percentages to one decimal place, and only at the end.

A measure from an earnings release that GAAP does not define is company-defined: label it, cite the release's reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP measure, and keep it out of GAAP tables.

Peers come from a person's list, or the same SIC code in the submissions data, with the rule recorded. Compare peers only on calendar-aligned periods, such as the frames API's, or list the pair as not comparable.

nouns.title: Reading risk factors
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

rules: Risk factors are in Item 1A of Form 10-K; a Form 10-Q reports material changes in Part II, Item 1A.
Quote each risk factor's heading exactly, with its form, accession number and section.
Group headings into fixed plain categories as a reading aid: market and demand, operations and supply, financial and liquidity, legal and regulatory, technology and security, people, other.
Compare with the prior year's filing by exact heading text: new, removed, reworded or unchanged. A reworded heading is matched by a person or a stated similarity rule, never silently.
Describe what the company says; never judge how likely a risk is or what it means for the share price.
Smaller reporting companies need not provide Item 1A; record the omission instead of inventing risks.

nouns.title: Building a dated catalyst calendar
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

rules: List only dated events from official sources: an earnings release or call the company announced, the annual meeting in its proxy statement, fiscal period ends, filing due dates, dividend dates the company declared, and debt maturities stated in its notes.
Mark an event confirmed when an official source states its date, or due by rule when a date is computed from a rule, and cite the rule.
Form 10-K is due 60 days after the fiscal year ends for large accelerated filers, 75 days for accelerated filers and 90 days for all other registrants.
Form 10-Q is due 40 days after each of the first three fiscal quarters for large accelerated and accelerated filers, and 45 days for all other registrants; no 10-Q is filed for the fourth quarter.
Form 8-K is due within four business days of most reportable events. An earnings release furnished under Item 2.02 carries the release's text as an exhibit, readable on EDGAR.
Flag a due-by-rule date that falls on a weekend or holiday for a person to check.
No rumors, forecasts, price levels or events no official source names.

nouns.title: Template: the company, the descriptive questions and the periods

value.describes: a research request: the company and any peers, the descriptive questions, the periods and forms to read, the date the research is as of, and what is out of scope
rules: Questions are descriptive.
out_of_scope lists advice, ratings, price targets and trades.

nouns.title: Template: the filings fetched and how each source was read

value.describes: a filing index: every source with its access method, the date its terms were read, the declared User-Agent, the request count and peak rate, and every filing with its form, accession, dates, address and digest
rules: peak_requests_per_second never exceeds 10 for the SEC; this pack's default limit is 2.

nouns.title: Template: metrics with the filing, period and unit behind every number

value.describes: a metric table: every reported fact with its concept, value, unit, period, form, accession and filed date; every derived value with its formula and cited inputs; and every restatement with both values and accessions
rules: Values are exactly as filed.
A derived value cites every input by fact_id.

nouns.title: Template: changes across periods and peers, each from two cited values

value.describes: a comparison: each metric across periods or against peers, every change computed from two cited values, and every pair that is not comparable listed with the reason
rules: percent_change is change over from_value times 100, rounded to one decimal; null when from_value is 0.

nouns.title: Template: risk factor headings quoted exactly, grouped and compared with the prior year

value.describes: a risk factor summary: each heading quoted exactly with its filing and section, a plain category, and whether it is new, removed, reworded or unchanged against the prior year's filing

nouns.title: Template: dated events from official sources, confirmed or due by rule

value.describes: a catalyst calendar: each dated event, whether an official source confirms it or a rule computes it, the source or rule, and a flag for dates a person should check
rules: A due-by-rule event cites its rule.
No event without an official source or a cited rule.

nouns.title: Template: a plain brief in which every number is cited, marked Not financial advice

value.describes: a cited brief: plain points that each cite fact, comparison, risk or event ids, the figures used with their units and facts, open questions, limits, and the notice Not financial advice
rules: Every point cites at least one id.
No advice, rating, price target or order.

nouns.title: Template: a different worker's review of every number and phrase in a brief

value.describes: a brief review by a worker other than the drafter: how many numbers were checked against their facts, every problem found, and whether it passed
rules: passed is true only when problems is empty.
numbers_checked counts the brief's figures plus the amounts and percentages in its points; dates and years are checked as dates.

nouns.title: Checklist a person runs before a brief is delivered
nouns.category_reason: A short checklist a person runs is part of the brief's guardrails.

items: The notice reads Not financial advice, and nothing reads as a recommendation, rating, target or order.
Every number traces to a filing, period, unit and accession, or to a formula over cited numbers.
Restated, derived and company-defined figures are labeled as such.
Peer comparisons use aligned periods, or say they are not comparable.
Every source was read as its terms permit, with the SEC's rate limit respected.
Any decision about money stays with the person who reads the brief.

verbs.title: Fetch the filings from official sources
verbs.summary: Fetch the filings a research request names from SEC EDGAR's documented APIs and archives, and from the company's own investor-relations pages, under each provider's terms, recording how each source was read and every document's digest.
verbs.outcome: A filing index, or blocked when a provider's terms forbid the reading.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent to declare: the requester's organization and its address, in the SEC's sample format.

max_rate_per_second.description: The most requests per second to the SEC.

network: Only the SEC's documented EDGAR endpoints on data.sec.gov and www.sec.gov, and the investor-relations pages the request names, read as their terms permit; never more than max_rate_per_second requests to the SEC, under a declared User-Agent; no logins, brokerage hosts or paid data feeds.
steps: Read each provider's terms first, and stop with blocked when they forbid automated reading.
Resolve each company's CIK from the SEC's ticker file, then fetch only the submissions, company facts and filing documents the request needs, caching every response.
Back off and slow down on a 403, a 429 or a rate-limit page; never disguise the client.
Record each source's access, terms date, request count and peak rate, and each document's SHA-256.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.filing-index's schema.
Every source records its access method and the date its terms were read.
Every SEC source's peak rate is at most max_rate_per_second.
Every filing belongs to a company and form the request names.

verbs.title: Extract metrics with the filing behind every number
verbs.summary: Extract the requested metrics from the company facts and filings with the concept, period, unit, form, accession and filed date behind each, derive margins, free cash flow and missing quarters by the metric rules, and record every restatement.
verbs.outcome: A metric table in which every number is cited.
steps: Copy each reported value exactly as filed, with its concept, unit, period and filing.
Derive each ratio, free cash flow and any missing fourth quarter by its formula over cited facts.
Use the latest filed value for a restated period and list the earlier one with both accessions.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.metric-table's schema.
Every fact equals the cited filing's value for its concept, unit and period.
Every derived value equals its formula over its inputs, with percentages rounded to one decimal.

verbs.title: Compare periods and peers
verbs.summary: Compare each metric with earlier periods and with the peers the request names, on aligned periods only, computing every change from two cited values.
verbs.outcome: A comparison in which every change is computed from cited values.

slots.name: metric_tables
slots.description: Pins of the company's and each peer's metric tables.

steps: Compare a period only with the same kind of period.
Compare peers only on calendar-aligned periods; list any other pair as not comparable, with why.
Describe differences; never rank companies as investments.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.comparison's schema.
Every change equals to_value minus from_value, and percent_change equals change over from_value times 100 rounded to one decimal, or null when from_value is 0.
Every peer comparison uses matching period ends, or is listed as not comparable.

verbs.title: Summarize the risk factors and what changed
verbs.summary: Quote each risk factor heading exactly with its filing and section, group the headings into plain categories, and say which are new, removed, reworded or unchanged against the prior year.
verbs.outcome: A risk factor summary with exact quotes.

slots.name: filing_index
slots.description: Pin of the filing index with this year's and last year's annual reports.

steps: Quote headings exactly; never paraphrase a heading as if quoting it.
Compare exact heading texts with the prior year's filing and state each status.
Record an omitted Item 1A instead of inventing risks.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.risk-factor-summary's schema.
Every heading appears character for character in the cited filing's Item 1A.
No summary judges how likely a risk is or what it means for the price.

verbs.title: Build a dated catalyst calendar
verbs.summary: List the dated events official sources name, such as results dates, filing deadlines, dividend dates and the annual meeting, each confirmed by its source or computed by a cited rule.
verbs.outcome: A catalyst calendar with no speculative events.
steps: Take confirmed dates only from official sources, and compute due dates only from cited rules.
Flag a computed date on a weekend or holiday for a person to check.
Leave out rumors, forecasts and price levels.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.catalyst-calendar's schema.
Every due-by-rule date equals its period end plus the days its cited rule sets.
Every confirmed event names an official source that states its date.

verbs.title: Write a cited brief, marked Not financial advice
verbs.summary: Write a plain brief from the metric table, comparison, risk factor summary and calendar in which every number is cited, every derived or company-defined figure is labeled, and the notice reads Not financial advice.
verbs.outcome: A cited brief with its notice.

slots.name: risk_factor_summary
slots.description: Pin of the risk factor summary.

steps: Cite fact, comparison, risk or event ids for every point.
Answer only the descriptive questions; turn any request for advice into a plain refusal and a pointer to the person who decides.
Run the brief checks and fix every failure before submitting.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.cited-brief's schema.
Every check in brief-checks passes on the brief.
Every cited id exists in the pinned inputs.
Points read plainly, without jargon a general reader would not know.

verbs.title: Review every number and phrase (a different worker)
verbs.summary: A worker other than the drafter checks every number in the brief against its cited fact or formula, and every phrase against the advice and order lists, and lists every problem.
verbs.outcome: A brief review that passes only with no problems.
steps: Recompute every number from its cited facts.
List every uncited number, advice or order phrase, stale period, unlabeled company-defined measure and any personal data.
Pass only when nothing is listed.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.brief-review's schema.
numbers_checked equals the brief's figures plus the amounts and percentages in its points.
The reviewing key differs from the drafting key.

verbs.title: Decide whether the reviewed brief is delivered (a person)
verbs.summary: A person reads the reviewed brief and its review and decides whether it is delivered to the requester inside the requester's scope; any decision about money stays with the reader.
verbs.outcome: A delivery record: delivered or held, with the reason.
steps: Deliver only a brief whose review passed.
Holding is a valid decision; give the reason.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.delivery-record's schema.
A deliver decision has review_passed true.
The submitting key belongs to a person who neither drafted nor reviewed the brief.
